answer: Before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it must lock scarce tokens in a vault; voting weight is proportional to locked stake, not account count. Newly locked tokens gain weight only after remaining bonded through a summit of several epochs, and proven double-voting burns the bond. An attacker may create unlimited identities, but splitting stake adds no influence; buying and immobilizing more tokens costs capital, foregone use, and risks slashing in a gale of coordinated fraud.
